title: Make the CLI a dependable surface for AI operators

needs: The CLI now has `--json` on the most useful commands for automation, but an AI still has to infer too much from scattered commands and report files. A first-time agent needs one canonical way to learn the project state, the available schemas, the reports that already exist, and what to do next.

`doctor --json`, `list --json`, `prune --json` and `run --json` do not yet share one error envelope. Refusals still expose translated human text as the only stable value in some paths, which makes an agent parse prose instead of identifiers.

Reports are deliberately JSON files under `work/ops`, but there is no CLI for listing, selecting or reading them. Agents can read the filesystem, but that makes the workflow depend on filename conventions rather than a product contract.

The report and operation formats are mostly discoverable by reading code, manifests and examples. That is workable for a human contributor and brittle for an AI operator, which should be able to ask the tool for the schema it is expected to obey.

There is no single `status` or `next` command that answers whether the active directory is a project, whether setup passes, whether reports exist, which operations are available, and what the next safe command is.
There is no short agent-oriented document that states the canonical commands, the `--json` preference, the report-first workflow, the `work/in` immutability rule, and how to attach Logics evidence.
context: Keep this a CLI and JSON contract change. Do not introduce an agent framework, MCP server, background daemon or new runtime dependency.
Machine identifiers are not translated. Human messages can stay localized, but JSON fields and error codes must be stable across locales.

The existing `scripts/selfcheck.py` plus thin pytest wrappers are the right test shape for this project. Each new machine contract needs one small check that fails if stdout stops being parseable JSON or a stable field disappears.
The CLI's existing exit codes are part of the contract and should not change. JSON reports the exit code; the process still returns it.

The tool already has the ingredients for `status`: `paths.resolve`, `doctor.check`, `manifests.discover`, and the reports under `work/ops`. The request is to expose them consistently, not to build a planner.
`next` should be advice, not automation. It names safe next commands and reasons; it does not run them.
Generated or runtime data under `work/` is not versioned. Docs and schemas must describe it without committing sample client paths.
acceptance_criteria: AC1: `meshanvil schema report --json`, `meshanvil schema operation --json`, and `meshanvil schema cli --json` print JSON schemas or schema-like contracts that are complete enough for an AI to validate reports, operation manifests and supported JSON CLI envelopes without reading Python source.

AC2: `meshanvil status --json` prints one JSON object containing project identity, setup state, operation summary, report summary, viewer hint, and next-action hints; stdout contains no human preamble.

AC3: `meshanvil reports --json`, `meshanvil reports --latest --json`, and `meshanvil reports <id> --json` let an agent list reports, find the latest report, and read one report without walking `work/ops` itself.

AC4: Every command that accepts `--json` returns the same top-level success and error envelope: success includes `ok: true`; failures include `ok: false`, `exit_code`, and a stable `error.code` plus a human `error.message`.

AC5: Refusals that an agent can act on have stable error codes, at least for unknown operation, missing source file, engine missing, target busy, invalid parameter, malformed `--set`, unreadable input format, and unavailable work directory.
AC6: `meshanvil next --json` returns ordered, safe next actions with reason codes and commands; it never starts a viewer, runs an operation, writes a report, or modifies a source file.

AC7: An agent-facing doc exists and states the canonical automation workflow: prefer `--json`, never write to `work/in`, discover before run, read reports rather than stdout, use `--evidence TASK:AC` when Logics is active, and keep client/source names out of committed docs.
AC8: Each new command and envelope rule has a selfcheck plus a thin pytest wrapper, and `make check`, `logics-manager lint --require-status`, and `logics-manager audit --group-by-doc` pass.

product.title: An agent-ready command surface for meshanvil
product.overview: Makes meshanvil usable by AI operators through explicit schemas, a single status view, report access commands, stable JSON errors, next-action advice and a short agent playbook, without adding an agent runtime.
goals: An AI can discover what meshanvil can do without reading Python source.
An AI can decide the next safe command from one status response.
An AI can list and read reports through a stable CLI contract instead of filesystem conventions.
JSON output stays parseable and stable across locales.
The human CLI remains friendly and unchanged unless `--json` is requested.
non_goals: No autonomous planner or agent framework.
No MCP server or background daemon.
No change to report semantics or operation execution.
No localization of machine identifiers or error codes.

backlog_items.title: Expose report operation and CLI schemas from the tool
problem: An agent has to infer the report, operation and CLI JSON shapes from source code and examples, which makes integration brittle and version-dependent.
scope_in: `meshanvil schema report --json` for the report object shape the viewer and runner expect.
`meshanvil schema operation --json` for operation manifests under `tools`.
`meshanvil schema cli --json` for the top-level CLI JSON success and error envelopes.
One selfcheck and pytest wrapper proving each schema command prints parseable JSON with required fields.
scope_out: A full external JSON Schema package dependency.
Runtime validation of every historical report during normal commands.
acceptance_criteria: AC1: Each schema subcommand prints JSON to stdout and no human preamble.
AC2: The report schema names required top-level report fields and the optional sections the viewer consumes.
AC3: The operation schema names required manifest fields, parameter field shapes and known parameter types.
AC4: The CLI schema describes the success envelope, error envelope and common command-specific payload fields.
AC5: `make check` fails if any schema command stops producing parseable JSON.

backlog_items.title: Add one status JSON command for agent preflight
problem: A first-time agent must call several commands and inspect files to know whether it is in a project, whether setup passes, what operations exist, and whether reports already exist.
scope_in: `meshanvil status --json` combining project resolution, `doctor.check`, `manifests.discover`, report counts and latest report metadata.
A viewer hint that says whether `meshanvil view` is a useful next action without starting it.
A small list of next-action hints, each with a stable reason code and a command string.
scope_out: Starting the viewer or running setup checks beyond what `doctor.check` already does.
A planner that chooses operation parameters.
Human table output; this command can be JSON-only initially.
acceptance_criteria: AC1: `status --json` prints one parseable object with `ok`, `project`, `doctor`, `operations`, `reports`, `viewer` and `next` keys.
AC2: The command exits with the same refused status as `doctor` when required setup is missing, while still printing the JSON object.
AC3: Report summary includes count and latest report id/path when present, but does not read every large artefact.
AC4: Next-action hints are ordered and include stable reason codes.
AC5: Selfcheck covers both a healthy and an unhealthy project.

backlog_items.title: Let agents list and read reports through the CLI
problem: Reports are the product's main record, but agents must currently walk `work/ops` and understand filename conventions to find or read them.
scope_in: `meshanvil reports --json` returning sorted report summaries.
`meshanvil reports --latest --json` returning the latest report object or a stable not-found error.
`meshanvil reports <id> --json` resolving ids like `003` and `003a` to the matching report file and returning its parsed JSON plus path metadata.
scope_out: Searching inside reports by arbitrary query.
acceptance_criteria: AC1: Report listing includes id, operation, status, path, input path when present, output path/state when present, and created/readable timestamp if available.
AC2: Latest report resolution is deterministic and matches current filename ordering rules.
AC3: Reading a report by id returns exactly one report or a stable ambiguous/not-found error.
AC4: Malformed report files are reported in the listing with a stable warning field rather than crashing the command.
AC5: Selfcheck covers empty, malformed, single-report and ambiguous-id cases.

backlog_items.title: Standardize JSON success and error envelopes
problem: The first `--json` pass made stdout parseable for the common path, but error payloads are not yet consistent across commands and some failures expose only prose.
scope_in: One helper for JSON success and error output used by every command that accepts `--json`.
Top-level `ok` on success and `ok`, `exit_code`, `error.code`, `error.message` on failure.
Preserving existing human stderr for non-JSON mode.
scope_out: Adding JSON mode to every command in this slice.
acceptance_criteria: AC1: All current `--json` commands use the same top-level envelope.
AC2: JSON-mode failures never print human-only text to stdout.
AC3: Non-JSON failures keep their current human output.
AC4: Selfcheck proves success and failure envelope shape for list, doctor, prune and run.

backlog_items.title: Give actionable refusals stable error codes
problem: An agent can recover from many refusals, but today it must parse translated text to distinguish missing files, unknown operations, invalid parameters and busy targets.
scope_in: Stable error codes for unknown operation, missing source file, engine missing, target busy, invalid parameter, malformed `--set`, unreadable input format and unavailable work directory.
A refusal representation that carries code plus human message without losing the current exception flow.
Mapping existing exception sources to codes at the boundary where the CLI prints JSON.
acceptance_criteria: AC1: Each named refusal has a stable code in JSON mode.
AC2: The human message remains present for logs and operators.
AC3: Codes are documented by `schema cli --json`.
AC4: Selfcheck covers at least one recovery path per named code without starting Blender.

backlog_items.title: Add a next action command that advises without acting
problem: Agents need a safe way to ask what to do next, but the product should not hide state changes behind advice.
scope_in: `meshanvil next --json` returning ordered action objects with reason codes, command strings and risk notes where needed.
Advice for no project marker, failed setup, no reports, reports present, no operations found, and viewer useful.
Shared status-gathering logic with `status --json` where that removes duplication.
scope_out: Picking operation parameters for a source file.
acceptance_criteria: AC1: `next --json` never modifies `work/`, starts a server, launches Blender, or writes reports.
AC2: Each action includes `reason`, `command` and `description` fields.
AC3: Advice is deterministic for the same project state.
AC4: Selfcheck covers at least no project marker, unhealthy setup, empty reports and existing reports.

backlog_items.title: Document the agent operating contract
problem: The project has contributor instructions, but no short operator-facing contract for AI tools that only need to use meshanvil safely.
scope_in: A short `docs/AI.md` or equivalent linked from the repository entry points.
Canonical command sequence: `status --json`, `schema ... --json`, `list --json`, `doctor --json`, `run ... --json`, `reports ... --json`.
Safety rules: do not write to `work/in`, do not commit `work/`, prefer report JSON over stdout, and keep client/source names out of docs.
Logics rule: use `--evidence TASK:AC` when implementing an active Logics task.
scope_out: Prompt templates for a specific vendor.
acceptance_criteria: AC1: The doc is under version control and linked from an obvious existing entry point.
AC2: It names the JSON commands and the report-first workflow.
AC3: It states safety and privacy rules for `work/`, `work/in` and committed docs.
AC4: It is short enough for an agent to load as context without replacing the full docs.

orchestration_task.title: Deliver the agent-ready CLI contract
plan: 1. Add the schema command first so the rest of the JSON contract has a place to document itself.
2. Factor the smallest shared JSON envelope helper and move current `--json` commands onto it without changing their exit codes.
3. Add stable refusal codes at the CLI boundary and cover the named recovery cases without launching Blender.
4. Add report listing, latest-report and report-by-id commands over `work/ops`, including malformed and ambiguous cases.
5. Add shared status collection and expose it through `status --json`.
6. Add `next --json` as a pure advice command that reuses status data and never mutates project state.
7. Write the short agent operating contract and link it from the repository's existing docs.
8. Add selfchecks and pytest wrappers for each new command and envelope rule, then run `make check`, Logics lint, audit and flow validate.
